questions.q: What does 'subject-oriented' mean in the classic data warehouse definition?
options: Data can only be queried by database administrators
Every table must have exactly one subject-matter expert assigned
Organized around business subjects like sales, customers, and products, not around the applications that created the data
Tables are organized alphabetically by name
questions.explain: Subject-orientation means the warehouse's structure reflects business concepts, not source-system quirks.

options: Every query must specify a time zone
Data is deleted automatically after one year
The warehouse only stores today's data
The warehouse preserves history, letting you ask what data looked like at a past point in time
questions.explain: Unlike an OLTP system that overwrites current state, a warehouse keeps historical snapshots anchored to specific dates.

questions.q: What does 'non-volatile' mean for a data warehouse?
options: Data disappears if the server loses power
Only volatile memory (RAM) is used to store the warehouse
The warehouse can never crash or go offline
Once loaded, data is appended rather than updated or deleted in place
questions.explain: Non-volatility is what makes historical reports consistent — the same query returns the same numbers every time.

options: It only accepts data typed in manually by an administrator
It stores raw, unprocessed exports from every source system separately
Integration refers only to third-party software integrations, not data
Data pulled from source systems is made consistent in naming, units, and format before it lands in the warehouse
questions.explain: Integration is about consistency — reconciling different sources into one coherent format.

questions.q: Where does the data in a warehouse actually originate?
options: Users type every row directly into the warehouse by hand
Data warehouses generate their own data independently of any source system
Warehouse data is generated randomly for testing purposes
It's fed by one or more OLTP systems (and sometimes external sources) through a periodic loading process — the warehouse doesn't originate data itself
questions.explain: A warehouse is downstream of transactional systems, reshaped for analysis rather than being the original system of record.
